description: SeleneArc é um simulador tático 3D para o desafio Lunar Landing Site Navigator. Cruzaremos topografia real da NASA (LOLA 80m/px), efemérides do JPL Horizons e mosaicos Moon Trek para prever energia solar, comunicação direta com a Terra (DTE) e impacto de atrasos de lançamento no Polo Sul lunar. Arquitetura e física já mapeadas em Rust/WASM e Next.js/Three.js. Buscamos pessoas interessadas.
summary: SeleneArc is a browser-native 3D lunar South Pole landing-window and launch-slip simulator built for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. At the Moon's South Pole, the Sun (0.53° disk) and Earth (~1.9° disk) skim within ±3° of the horizon with zero atmosphere while Earth traces a ±7° libration loop—meaning a single mountain ridge decides whether a mission keeps solar power and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio lock or freezes in a -234 °C blackout. When a rocket launch slips by just 9 days on Earth, moving mountain shadows can turn a sunlit landing zone into a fatal trap. Fusing official NASA LRO LOLA 80 m/px (0.64 ha/px) elevation rasters, JPL Horizons DE441 ephemerides solved with 3D topocentric parallax in Rust/WebAssembly, NOAA GOES-18 space weather feeds, and Moon Trek WMTS mosaics, SeleneArc dynamically re-ranks 17 South Pole landing sites across +0 to +30 day launch delays in < 3 ms, plans safe < 15° A* rover routes, exports tactile .STL 3D crater models for blind students, and runs at $0.00 cloud cost.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

SeleneArc places mission planners, flight directors, and students directly on the lunar landing pad to evaluate how +0 to +30 day launch delays reshape sunlight, radio communications, and surface hazards across 17 Lunar South Pole targets (all 9 updated Oct 2024 Artemis III candidate regions plus 8 historical, robotic, polar rim, and negative-control benchmarks).

- 360° Topocentric Horizon & LOLA Terrain Pipeline: Offline Python scripts process NASA GSFC PGDA Product 90 LOLA Digital Elevation & Slope GeoTIFFs (80 m/px = 0.64 ha/pixel) in the canonical IAU MOON_ME frame (R = 1,737.4 km), slicing them into compact 360 KB binary patches and curvature-compensated 360° mountain horizon masks.

- Rust -> WebAssembly 3D Physics Kernel (< 3 ms): Executes exact 3D topocentric vector subtraction v_topo = P_target(t) - R_site(lat, lon, h) against NASA JPL Horizons DE441 ephemerides. This eliminates the +0.26° geocentric parallax error of smooth-sphere models (verified across 12 JPL Horizons Golden Oracles with 0.0002° solar azimuth and 0.0007° solar elevation accuracy).

- Full Mission Simulation Workstation: Computes finite-disk solar penumbra (0.53°), 26.5 GHz Ka-band Direct-to-Earth link budgets with knife-edge Fresnel diffraction and ITU-R P.618 rain attenuation across NASA's 3 DSN complexes (Goldstone, Madrid, Canberra), 1,000-trial 3-sigma Monte Carlo powered descent hazard clearance (< 9 ms), A* rover pathfinding (< 15° grade to water-ice traps), 3D Artemis Base Camp cryogenic microgrid routing, NOAA GOES-18 solar proton event (SPE) radiation dosimetry with LOLA 360° sky-view and regolith shielding, and JPL Lunar NEO asteroid impact flux (cad.api?body=Moon).

2. Key Benefits & Intended Impact

- Mission Readiness & Safety: Prevents mission-ending thermal and communications blackouts caused by launch scrubs. On a +9 day launch delay, dynamic site pivoting with customizable Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) weights preserves +18 readiness points and +121 hours of continuous sunlight compared to a static baseline site.

- Universal & Tactile STEM Inclusion: Features a 1-click watertight .STL 3D crater exporter with embossed rover paths so blind and low-vision students can feel Shackleton Crater by touch, alongside an interactive 3D Lunar Physics Theater (Educator Mode), Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe telemetry palette, EN/PT-BR bilingual interface, and 1-click Flight-Readiness PDF Dossier export.

- Zero-Cost Scalability ($0.00/mo): By running heavy ray-marching and Monte Carlo physics client-side in WebAssembly and caching public NASA/JPL/NOAA endpoints at the Cloudflare edge (caches.default), hundreds of classrooms and mission analysts can run simulations simultaneously at zero server cost.

3. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Core Physics Engine: Rust compiled to WebAssembly (wasm-bindgen, Cargo).

- Frontend & 3D Visualization: Next.js 16 (Static Export), React 19, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei), custom GLSL shaders (Hapke bidirectional lunar reflectance), and Tailwind CSS.

- Edge & Data Pipeline: Cloudflare Pages & Workers (Cache API), Python 3 (rasterio, numpy) for GeoTIFF processing, and SIL Open Font License 1.1 typography (Space Grotesk & Inter).

4. How Our Project Is Creative & Factors Considered

Rather than building another static top-down map viewer, we inverted the camera to the lander's eye level (including a first-person 1.80 m xEMU astronaut visor with gold glare filtering) and coupled orbital mechanics, 3D topography, RF diffraction, cryogenic survival, radiation shielding, and tactile accessibility into a single < 3 ms real-time loop. Our team carefully accounted for reference-frame consistency (preventing 0.03° MOON_PA vs. MOON_ME drift), finite solar/Earth angular diameters, sensor resolution limits (explicitly flagging sub-pixel boulders below LOLA's 80 m/px grid), and 3-layer offline resilience.
